name: Hyperpigmentation
description: Hyperpigmentation is a skin condition characterized by patches of skin that are darker in color than the surrounding area. This occurs due to an overproduction of melanin, which is responsible for skin pigmentation.
causes: Inflammation from acne or other skin conditions
symptoms: Discolored areas after healing of cuts, burns, or inflamed skin
risk_factors: Use of certain medications (e.g., birth control pills, corticosteroids)
History of skin damage such as acne scars
Dark skinned individuals are more prone to hyperpigmentation

daily_routine.step: Cleanse your skin gently with a mild cleanser.
daily_routine.purpose: Remove dirt and impurities from the skin.

daily_routine.step: Apply a broad-spectrum sunscreen with at least SPF 30 daily, even on cloudy days.
daily_routine.purpose: Protect against UV rays that can exacerbate hyperpigmentation.

daily_routine.step: Use a brightening serum or moisturizer containing recommended ingredients like hydroquinone or vitamin C.
daily_routine.purpose: Even out skin tone and reduce the appearance of dark patches.

natural_remedies: Apply aloe vera gel to soothe irritated skin.
Use licorice root extract as it contains properties that help lighten the skin.
lifestyle_tips: Wear protective clothing, such as hats and long sleeves, when outdoors.
Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water.
Maintain a healthy diet rich in antioxidants.
common_myths: Hyperpigmentation can be completely avoided by staying out of the sun.
All hyperpigmented spots are benign and won't change or spread.
when_to_consult_doctor: Seek professional help if your pigmentation is severe, rapidly changing, or accompanied by other symptoms like redness, scaling, or itching.
prevention: Protect skin from sun exposure with clothing and hats
Avoid picking at the skin to prevent inflammation

severity_levels.mild: Visible but not prominent hyperpigmentation that may cover a small area of the skin.
severity_levels.moderate: Darker patches on the skin that are more noticeable and can cover larger areas, such as the cheeks or forehead.
severity_levels.severe: Widespread dark patches that significantly affect overall appearance and may be accompanied by inflammation.

expert_tips: Consistency is key in treating hyperpigmentation. Products should be used regularly for best results.
Always patch test new products before applying them to a larger area of the skin.
